nodes.label:
Student Has a
Coding Question
nodes.title: Student Has a Coding Question
nodes.info: Something is not working, is not understood, or is ready for a second look.

nodes.label:
What Kind of
Help Is Needed?
nodes.title: What Kind of Help Is Needed?
nodes.info: Routes to one of three coding-help agents based on the actual need.

nodes.label:
AI Assisted
Debugging Help
nodes.title: AI Assisted Debugging Help
nodes.info: Suggests where a bug might be. It never fixes the code directly -- the student still makes the change.

nodes.label:
AI Tutor for
Students
nodes.title: AI Tutor for Students
nodes.info: Asks a guiding question back rather than stating the answer, so the student arrives at it themselves.

nodes.label:
AI Code Review
Assistant
nodes.title: AI Code Review Assistant
nodes.info: Flags style-level issues before a peer code review session begins, so human review time goes to substance rather than formatting.

nodes.label:
Mentor Present
and Available
nodes.title: Mentor Present and Available
nodes.info: A mentor stays in the room for all three, ready to step in if the hint, suggestion, or flag is not landing.

nodes.label:
Student Does the Actual
Fixing, Answering, or Revising
nodes.title: Student Does the Actual Fixing, Answering, or Revising
nodes.info: The agent points; the student does the work. Any path where the agent produces the finished answer has failed, however good the answer is.
